description: Divergence allowlist: corpus entries where dentaku-ts intentionally differs from Ruby dentaku 3.5.7, each justified by an ADR or a PLAN.md/issue-spec decision. The oracle runner (issue 014) asserts the TS-side `expected` outcome for listed entries and fails on any entry that stops diverging (stale). Seeded by issue 002; completed by issue 014.

entrySchema.formula: string — must equal a corpus entry's formula exactly
entrySchema.vars: object, optional (default {}) — must equal the corpus entry's vars exactly; (formula, vars) identifies the entry
entrySchema.reason: one of "ADR-0003.1"…"ADR-0003.5" | "ADR-0004" | "ADR-0001" (fixed 20-digit Decimal precision vs Ruby's variable-precision BigDecimal/Float results) | "PLAN-additions" (deliberate dentaku-ts semantic additions recorded in PLAN.md or an issue spec)
entrySchema.expected: TS-side outcome: a TS error class name string, or an encoded result object using the corpus result encoding
entrySchema.note: string, optional — reviewer context (what Ruby did and why TS differs)

entries.note: Ruby raises Dentaku::ArgumentError when no WHEN matches and there is no ELSE; TS CASE is total and returns null (docs/issues/006: 'no match, no else -> null', SQL CASE semantics; tested in tests/evaluator.spec.ts)

Ruby BigDecimal#power carries ~44 significant digits here; TS decimal.js is pinned to precision 20 (src/decimal.ts, PLAN.md), and the (x^-0.1)-1 cancellation surfaces the truncation. Values agree to 17 significant digits
Ruby BigDecimal division emits 30 significant digits for 400/0.6; TS decimal.js is pinned to precision 20. Same value, different repeating-digit cutoff
Ruby coerces the string context value "1" to a number and returns -2; TS removes string->number coercion in arithmetic
Ruby coerces "-1" and returns 1; TS rejects negation of a string
Ruby coerces "-1" and returns 0
Ruby coerces "1" and returns -2
Ruby BigDecimal division emits 29 significant digits for 2024/1/6; TS decimal.js is pinned to precision 20. Same value, different repeating-digit cutoff
Ruby downcases identifiers, so N resolves to the n binding and returns 42; TS identifiers are case-sensitive
Ruby downcases context keys, so N binds n and returns 42; TS identifiers are case-sensitive
Ruby BigDecimal division emits 30 significant digits for 400/0.6; TS decimal.js is pinned to precision 20. Same value, different repeating-digit cutoff

Ruby treats the numeric item.value 1 as truthy and proceeds to the second item, whose missing key raises UnboundVariableError; TS requires the ALL body to produce a boolean and fails on the first item
Ruby treats the numeric item.value 1 as truthy and short-circuits to true; TS requires the ANY body to produce a boolean
Ruby's Function.numeric cast coerces the string context value "2.3" and returns 1.7; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby treats the nil predicate as false and returns 0; TS requires a boolean predicate
Ruby treats the nil predicate as false and returns 2; TS requires a boolean predicate
Ruby treats the null literal predicate as false and returns 2; TS requires a boolean predicate
Ruby's intercept computes through Float (16 significant digits); TS computes the same regression exactly in Decimal at precision 20. Values agree to Float precision
Ruby's Function.numeric cast coerces "2.3" and returns 2.3; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby's Function.numeric cast coerces "0.3" and returns 0.3; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby treats nil as false and returns true; TS requires a boolean operand

Ruby's `=` answers false for mixed-type pairs (1 = "1" is false, so Ruby returns true via "2" = "2"); TS makes mixed-type (in)equality a type error (no coercion between operand types, src/ast/equality.ts)
Ruby's `=` answers false for the mixed-type pair and returns false; TS makes mixed-type equality a type error
Ruby coerces both string context values and returns 1.845; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby coerces "1.8453" (nil places means 0) and returns 2; TS rejects the string argument

Ruby coerces "1.8453" (nil places means 0) and returns 1; TS rejects the string argument

Ruby's Function.numeric cast coerces "2.3" and returns 5.1; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby's Function.numeric cast coerces "2.3" and returns 12.3; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby's `+` concatenates arrays (Array#+); TS arithmetic takes numeric operands only — the array concat/difference behavior is tightened away at eval time (src/ast/operands.ts)
Ruby's `-` computes the array difference (Array#-); TS arithmetic takes numeric operands only
Ruby coerces the string context values and returns 5; TS removes string->number coercion in arithmetic

Ruby (with the mul pack loaded) coerces "2.3" and returns 46; TS numeric function arguments must already be numbers
Ruby coerces the date-shaped string to a Time at eval and returns 2023-02-01; TS removes eval-time string->date coercion (dates require DATE() or date-typed context values)
Ruby coerces the date-shaped string to a Time at eval and returns 2022-12-01; TS removes eval-time string->date coercion
Ruby coerces both date-shaped strings to Times and returns 1 (days); TS removes eval-time string->date coercion
